title: Single-Function Reentrancy
summary: An ETH bank sends funds with a low-level call before it zeroes the caller's balance. A malicious recipient re-enters withdraw() from its receive() and drains the bank.
web2Analog: A TOCTOU / double-spend race: state is read and acted on before it is updated, so a re-entrant caller acts on stale state.

identify.question: What makes withdraw() reentrant?
options: It reads balanceOf into a local variable
It sends ETH (an external call) BEFORE setting the balance to zero
identify.explanation: withdraw() does the external call (msg.sender.call) before `balanceOf[msg.sender] = 0`. This violates checks-effects-interactions: during the call the balance is still non-zero, so the recipient can re-enter and withdraw again.

hints: Look at the ORDER of operations in withdraw(): when exactly is the balance set to zero?
An attacker contract's receive() runs DURING the external call — what is the balance at that moment?
From receive(), call bank.withdraw() again while the bank still holds funds.
The fix is checks-effects-interactions (zero the balance before the call) or a nonReentrant guard.
